content:
The Permutations & Combinations chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Permutations & Combinations tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Permutations & Combinations

Arrangements and selections, circular permutations, arrangements with repetition and the fundamental counting principle.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • ⁿPᵣ = n!/(n−r)! (order matters); ⁿCᵣ = n!/(r!(n−r)!) (order doesn’t).
  • n distinct in a row: n!; in a circle: (n−1)!.
  • r places filled from n with repetition: nʳ.
  • ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₙ₋ᵣ; ΣⁿCᵣ = 2ⁿ.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Using permutations where order does not matter (or vice versa).
  • Using n! instead of (n−1)! for circular arrangements.
  • Double counting identical items.

quiz.title: CAT Permutations & Combinations Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten CAT-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: A person has 4 shirts and 3 pairs of trousers. In how many ways can he dress himself?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: By the Fundamental Counting Principle, the number of ways = (ways to choose shirt) × (ways to choose trousers).
Step 2: = 4 × 3 = 12.
Answer: 12

questions.q: In how many ways can 4 different books be arranged on a shelf?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: This is the number of permutations of 4 distinct objects = 4!
Step 2: 4! = 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24.
Answer: 24

questions.q: How many 3-letter words (with or without meaning) can be formed from the letters A, B, C, D, E without repetition?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: We need to arrange 3 letters chosen from 5 distinct letters without repetition = 5P3.
Step 2: 5P3 = 5 × 4 × 3 = 60.
Answer: 60

questions.q: In how many ways can 3 students be selected from a group of 7?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Order does not matter, so we need 7C3.
Step 2: 7C3 = 7! / (3! × 4!) = (7 × 6 × 5) / (3 × 2 × 1) = 210 / 6 = 35.
Answer: 35

questions.q: In how many ways can the letters of the word MATHS be arranged?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: MATHS has 5 distinct letters.
Step 2: Number of arrangements = 5! = 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120.
Answer: 120

questions.q: In how many ways can 5 people be seated around a circular table?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: For circular permutations of n objects, one position is fixed and the rest are arranged: (n-1)!
Step 2: (5-1)! = 4! = 24.
Answer: 24

questions.q: How many 2-digit numbers can be formed using the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 without repetition?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Choose the tens digit: 5 options. Choose the units digit from remaining 4: 4 options.
Step 2: Total = 5 × 4 = 20.
Answer: 20

faq.a: Use permutation when the order matters (arrangements) and combination when it does not (selections).
Rotations of the same circular arrangement are identical, so we fix one position — giving (n−1)!.
